The g-mesh implementations query returned 18 types, and a repo-wide grep for `WriteContentType` methods found the same 18.

`TestRender` is a test double, and its `WriteContentType` is an empty no-op.

I did not count `HTMLProduction` and `HTMLDebug`. They implement the separate `HTMLRender` interface (which has an `Instance` method), not `Render`.

The interface is `render.Render`, declared in `render/render.go:10`. It requires `Render(http.ResponseWriter) error` and `WriteContentType(w http.ResponseWriter)`. Searching the whole repository, I found 16 types in `render/` and one test type in the root package that define both methods.

**In the `render` package (production types):**

| Type | File |

**Outside `render/`:**
- `TestRender` is in `context_test.go` (`Render` at line 1043, `WriteContentType` at line 1047). It is a test-only stub with pointer receivers, so `*TestRender` satisfies the interface.

**What I checked:**
- All 17 types above have both methods. I matched receivers with or without a name, since `Redirect` and `TestRender` use unnamed ones.
- No struct embeds `Render`, so no type satisfies the interface only through embedding.
- `Context.Render` in `context.go` is a method that takes a `render.Render`. It is not an implementation.

`HTMLProduction` and `HTMLDebug` in `render/html.go` are not implementations. They implement the separate `HTMLRender` interface, which has an `Instance` method.

`Binding` is declared in two places, both in package `binding`:

1. `binding/binding.go:32` has `type Binding interface`. The file is built under `//go:build !nomsgpack`, so this is the default build.
2. `binding/binding_nomsgpack.go:30` has `type Binding interface`. The file is built under `//go:build nomsgpack`, so this is the variant used when msgpack support is excluded.

The two declarations are mutually exclusive build-tag variants. Only one is compiled in any given build, so they don't conflict.

`Binding` is declared in two places, both in the `binding` package:

1. `binding/binding.go:32` is built with `//go:build !nomsgpack`, which is the default build.
2. `binding/binding_nomsgpack.go:30` is built with `//go:build nomsgpack`.

The two declarations are identical:

```go
type Binding interface {
    Name() string
    Bind(*http.Request, any) error
}
```

The build tags are mutually exclusive, so only one file is compiled in any given build. The duplication exists because the `nomsgpack` variant leaves out the msgpack MIME constants (`MIMEMSGPACK` and `MIMEMSGPACK2`). The rest of each file, including `BindingBody` and `BindingUri`, is duplicated the same way. If you change the interface, change it in both files.

The method is `(*Context).Abort` in `context.go:206`. It sets the abort index so no remaining handlers in the chain run.

These are the non-test functions that call it directly:

| Caller | File | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `Context.AbortWithStatus` | `context.go` | 212 |
| `Context.AbortWithStatusPureJSON` | `context.go` | 221 |
| `Context.AbortWithStatusJSON` | `context.go` | 229 |
| `Context.Render` | `context.go` | 1151 |
| `CustomRecoveryWithWriter` | `recovery.go` | 52 |

Each of these needs updating for the new signature. The line numbers are where each caller function starts, not the exact call line.

`TestContextIsAborted` in `context_test.go` (line 1800) also calls it, but I left it out of the list because you asked for non-test code only. It will need updating too.

The `find_references` results matched the `find_callers` results row for row. Every row was resolved, so there are no indirect or callback-only usages that a caller-only search would miss.

`AbortWithError` isn't a direct caller. It goes through `AbortWithStatus`, so it inherits any change there.

The method is `func (c *Context) Abort()` at `context.go:207`. It sets `c.index = abortIndex`, so `Next()` skips the remaining handlers.

A search of non-test source found five direct call sites, in five functions:

| Calling function | Location |
|---|---|
| `Context.AbortWithStatus` | `context.go:216` |
| `Context.AbortWithStatusPureJSON` | `context.go:223` |
| `Context.AbortWithStatusJSON` | `context.go:231` |
| `Context.Render` | `context.go:1164` (after `c.Error(err)` when rendering fails) |
| the `CustomRecoveryWithWriter` middleware closure | `recovery.go:84` (broken-pipe branch, after `c.Error(err)`) |

- **Other callers:** No other non-test file calls `Abort()`. That includes the `binding`, `render`, `ginS` and `internal` packages, and `gin.go`. Nothing calls it through a method value or alias either.
- **Doc comments:** The comments above `AbortWithStatus`, `AbortWithStatusPureJSON` and `AbortWithStatusJSON` mention `Abort()` in backticks. The `Abort` doc comment itself (`context.go:203-206`) describes the authorization use case. Update these if the new signature changes their meaning.
- **Tests and examples:** I excluded `_test.go` files, as you asked. Any test that calls `Abort()` will also break. Docs or README code samples may too, since I only searched Go source. I can list those if you want.

**Handler method:** `Engine.ServeHTTP` (`gin.go:661`) satisfies `http.Handler`. It calls `Engine.updateRouteTrees`, `responseWriter.reset` and `Context.reset`. It then hands the request to `Engine.handleHTTPRequest`, which is the internal dispatch function.

**Functions `Engine.handleHTTPRequest` (`gin.go:689`) calls directly:**

| Callee | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `cleanPath` | `path.go:22` | Normalizes the request path. |
| `node.getValue` | `tree.go:417` | Walks the routing tree to find the matching handlers and params. |
| `Context.Next` | `context.go:187` | Runs the matched handler chain. |
| `responseWriter.WriteHeaderNow` | `response_writer.go:76` | Flushes the response header after the handlers run. |
| `redirectTrailingSlash` | `gin.go:780` | Fallback when no route matches: redirects to add or remove the trailing slash. |
| `redirectFixedPath` | `gin.go:807` | Fallback when no route matches: redirects to the case-insensitive or cleaned path. |
| `serveError` | `gin.go:763` | Fallback when no route matches: writes the 404 or 405 response. |
| `strings.Join` | `gin.go:751` | Standard library. Its edge is `resolved: false`, but it is a stdlib call, not a repo function. |

The tool also reported some non-call references in `gin.go` and `context.go`. I didn't inspect them, so I can't say what they are.

`Engine.ServeHTTP` (`gin.go:662`) satisfies `http.Handler`. After it sets up a pooled `Context`, it calls `engine.handleHTTPRequest(c)` (`gin.go:672`). That function (`gin.go:690`) walks the routing tree and dispatches to the matched handlers.

## Direct calls in `handleHTTPRequest` (`gin.go:690-760`)

**Path preparation**
- `c.Request.URL.EscapedPath()` (line 696), used when `UseEscapedPath` is set.
- `cleanPath(rPath)` (line 704), used when `RemoveExtraSlash` is set.

**Tree lookup and dispatch**
- `root.getValue(rPath, c.params, c.skippedNodes, unescape)` (line 715) looks up the route in the method's tree.
- `c.Next()` (line 722) runs the matched handler chain.
- `c.writermem.WriteHeaderNow()` (line 723) flushes the header after the handlers finish.

**No route found: redirect helpers**
- `redirectTrailingSlash(c)` (line 728), when `value.tsr` is true and `RedirectTrailingSlash` is enabled.
- `redirectFixedPath(c, root, engine.RedirectFixedPath)` (line 731), when `RedirectFixedPath` is enabled.

**No route found: 405 handling** (when `HandleMethodNotAllowed` is set)
- `make(...)` (line 741) allocates the `allowed` slice.
- `tree.root.getValue(rPath, nil, c.skippedNodes, unescape)` (line 746) checks the other methods' trees.
- `append(...)` (line 747) collects the methods that match.
- `strings.Join(allowed, ", ")` (line 752) builds the value for the `Allow` header.
- `c.writermem.Header().Set("Allow", ...)` (line 752) sets that header.
- `serveError(c, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, default405Body)` (line 753) writes the 405 response.

**Final fallback (404)**
- `serveError(c, http.StatusNotFound, default404Body)` (line 759).

`len(...)` is also called in several places.

## What the helpers do
- `serveError` (`gin.go:764`) sets the status and calls `c.Next()` so the `allNoRoute` or `allNoMethod` handlers can run. If nothing was written and the status is unchanged, it writes the default body as `text/plain`. Otherwise it calls `WriteHeaderNow()`.
- `redirectTrailingSlash` (`gin.go:781`) rewrites `req.URL.Path` to add or remove the trailing slash, taking `X-Forwarded-Prefix` into account. It then calls `redirectRequest(c)`.

- `gin.go`

The only other importer is `binding/json_test.go`, which I left out because it's a test file.

resultText:
Use **`Recovery()`**, defined in `recovery.go` (line 35).

Its doc comment says it "returns a middleware that recovers from any panics and writes a 500 if there was one." It writes errors to `DefaultErrorWriter`. Add it with `router.Use(gin.Recovery())`.

Related variants in the same file:
- `CustomRecovery(handle RecoveryFunc)` lets you supply your own panic handler.
- `RecoveryWithWriter(out io.Writer, ...)` lets you choose the log writer.

The middleware is **`Recovery()`**, defined in `recovery.go` at line 35. Add it with `router.Use(gin.Recovery())`. It catches panics from downstream handlers, logs them, and responds with HTTP 500.

`recovery.go` also defines these variants:
- `CustomRecovery(handle RecoveryFunc)` (line 40) lets you supply your own panic-handling function.
- `RecoveryWithWriter(out io.Writer, ...)` (line 45) writes the panic logs to a writer you choose.
- `CustomRecoveryWithWriter(out, handle)` (line 53) combines both.

`gin.Default()` already includes `Recovery()` (along with `Logger()`), so you only need to add it yourself if you build the engine with `gin.New()`.

`HandlerFunc` is declared in `gin.go:50` as `type HandlerFunc func(*Context)`. `HandlersChain` (`gin.go:56`) is a slice of it.

Seven other non-test source files reference it. The counts are references to the type, per file:

| File | Refs | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `routergroup.go` | 26 | `IRoutes` and `IRouter` interface methods (`Use`, `Handle`, `Any`, `Match`, `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE`/`PATCH`/`PUT`/`OPTIONS`/`HEAD`, `Group`). The same methods on `RouterGroup`, plus `createStaticHandler`. |
| `ginS/gins.go` | 13 | Package-level wrappers: `Group`, `Handle`, `NoRoute`, `NoMethod`, `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `Any`. |
| `logger.go` | 6 | `Logger`, `LoggerWithWriter`, `LoggerWithConfig`, `ErrorLoggerT`. |
| `recovery.go` | 4 | `Recovery`, `RecoveryWithWriter`, `CustomRecovery`, `CustomRecoveryWithWriter`. |
| `auth.go` | 3 | `BasicAuth`, `BasicAuthForProxy`. |
| `utils.go` | 3 | `Bind`, `WrapF`, `WrapH`. |
| `context.go` | 1 | `Context.Handler`, which returns the handler. |

Other places in `gin.go` also use the type. They are `Engine.NoRoute`, `Engine.NoMethod` and `Engine.Use`, plus the `RouteInfo` struct (`gin.go:67`) and `HandlersChain.Last`.

Test files also reference it, and they will break too: `gin_test.go`, `context_test.go` and `routergroup_test.go`.

- **Complete list:** The `find_references` result was paginated (`hasMore: true`), but the per-file tally covers the whole reference set, so the file list is complete. The rows I read out above come from the first page only, so the method lists may be incomplete.
- **Indirect uses:** The tool tracks references to the type name only. Code that builds handlers as plain `func(*gin.Context)` literals, without naming `HandlerFunc`, won't show up. Those would need a separate search if you change the signature.

The type is `HandlerFunc`, declared at `gin.go:51` as `type HandlerFunc func(*Context)`. It has a companion type, `HandlersChain []HandlerFunc` (`gin.go:57`), and any change to `HandlerFunc` also changes that slice type.

I searched non-test `.go` files for `HandlerFunc`, `HandlersChain` and the raw `func(*Context)` form. I did not search non-Go files such as docs or README code samples.

## Files that reference it (besides the declaration)

**`gin.go`** (the declaration file, with more uses further down)
- `HandlersChain.Last()` returns `HandlerFunc` (line 60).
- `RouteInfo.HandlerFunc` is a struct field (line 72).
- `Engine` has `allNoRoute`, `allNoMethod`, `noRoute` and `noMethod` fields of type `HandlersChain` (lines 179-182).
- `NoRoute`, `NoMethod` and `Use` take `...HandlerFunc` (lines 326, 332, 340).
- `addRoute` takes a `HandlersChain` (line 364).
- `Routes()` reads `root.handlers.Last()` into `RouteInfo` (lines 400-405).

**`routergroup.go`** (the most uses)
- The `IRoutes` interface lists `...HandlerFunc` in `Use`, `Handle`, `Any`, `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `OPTIONS`, `HEAD` and `Match` (lines 29-45). `Group` on `IRouter` takes it too. Anything implementing these interfaces outside the repo would break as well.
- `RouterGroup.Handlers` is a `HandlersChain` field (line 56).
- The same methods on `RouterGroup` take `...HandlerFunc` (lines 65-156).
- `handle` and `combineHandlers` use `HandlersChain` (lines 86, 241, 244).
- `staticFileHandler` takes a `HandlerFunc` (line 181).
- `createStaticHandler` returns a `HandlerFunc` (line 216).

**`context.go`**
- `Context.handlers` is a `HandlersChain` field (line 67).
- `Handler()` returns `HandlerFunc` (line 167).
- **Call site:** `Next()` invokes `c.handlers[c.index](c)` (line 192). This is where a second argument would have to be supplied.

**`tree.go`**
- `node.handlers` is a `HandlersChain` field (line 106).
- `addRoute` and `insertChild` take a `HandlersChain` (lines 135, 288).
- `nodeValue.handlers` is a `HandlersChain` field (line 401).

**`debug.go`**
- `debugPrintRoute` takes a `HandlersChain` (line 32).

**`auth.go`**
- `BasicAuthForRealm`, `BasicAuth` and `BasicAuthForProxy` return `HandlerFunc` (lines 48, 72, 98). Their returned closures are `func(c *Context)` literals that would need the new signature.

**`logger.go`**
- `ErrorLogger`, `ErrorLoggerT`, `Logger`, `LoggerWithFormatter`, `LoggerWithWriter` and `LoggerWithConfig` return `HandlerFunc` (lines 207-245).

**`recovery.go`**
- `Recovery`, `CustomRecovery`, `RecoveryWithWriter` and `CustomRecoveryWithWriter` return `HandlerFunc` (lines 35-53).

**`utils.go`**
- `Bind`, `WrapF` and `WrapH` return `HandlerFunc` (lines 29, 47, 54). `WrapF` and `WrapH` adapt `http.HandlerFunc` and `http.Handler`, so their wrapper closures need updating.

**`ginS/gins.go`** (the singleton-engine wrapper package)
- `NoRoute`, `NoMethod`, `Group`, `Handle`, `POST`, `GET`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `OPTIONS`, `HEAD`, `Any` and `Use` all take `...gin.HandlerFunc` (lines 40-124).

## Other places to check

- **Call sites:** the only place a handler is actually invoked is `context.go:192`. `Engine.Routes()` only reads and stores the handler, so it needs no change beyond the type.
- **Middleware closures:** any function returning `HandlerFunc` has a `func(c *Context)` literal inside it, in `auth.go`, `logger.go`, `recovery.go`, `utils.go` and `routergroup.go`. These literals are the functions you'd have to rewrite. Because they are literals, the type name alone won't find them.
- **Non-test code outside the root package:** `ginS/gins.go` was the only one my search found. I didn't find any in `binding/`, `render/` or `internal/`.
- **Test files and examples:** I excluded test files as requested. They will fail to compile after the change, so expect many edits there (`*_test.go`, plus `ginS/gins_test.go`).
